name: claude_brain_surgery_story
source: Source: Exin Therapeutics, as reported by The Decoder, Digital Citizen & others (Nov 2026). Company claims, not peer-reviewed.

lines.text: This tiny mouse just had brain surgery.
And no human chose the treatment.
A startup gave an AI nineteen gene therapies,
one robotic needle, and one goal: stop this mouse's seizures.
So which therapy would you pick?
The AI picked this one: a therapy that boosts the brain's natural brakes.
The first Claude model planned the surgery... and then refused to guide the needle.
So they switched to another Claude model.
A vet opened the skull, and the AI steered the needle in,
injecting a droplet smaller than a pinhead.
Then two other AIs got the exact same task.
Each one picked a different treatment.
The mouse recovered. But did it work? Nobody knows yet.
Would you let an AI choose your treatment?
